- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high or 1.5x recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in upward correction — adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >1.2x recent 14-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overestimates volatility — use 1.1x historical volatility multiplier for smoothing.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction, not absolute magnitude.
